what_changed: Attempt 1's file already SAID maximum per-query WALL time; its sweep populated the statistic from the helper's internal engine time instead, so the gate did not compute the metric it had frozen. NO THRESHOLD IS CHANGED HERE. The selector now consumes wall milliseconds, engine time is retained as a descriptive field only, and both are persisted per query. The recorded attempt-1 wall maxima already select the same depth, so this correction is not a re-tuning after seeing results -- it makes the code compute what the file always specified.
note: No games are authorized by this document. The endpoint screen it describes is FROZEN, NOT EXECUTED.

engine_settings.mdTime_excluded: wall-clock search mode is excluded: mdFixedPly=false sets maxPly=Integer.MAX_VALUE and terminates on elapsed time, which is not reproducible
engine_settings.depth_4_behaviour: FindMove.internalComputeMove iterates currentMaxPly from 3 and executes a depth only when (currentMaxPly != 4 || currentMaxPly == maxPly). Depth 4 RUNS when it is the requested terminal depth and is SKIPPED only as an intermediate iteration. Executed ladders: 3 -> {3}; 4 -> {3,4}; 5 -> {3,5}; 6 -> {3,5,6}; 7 -> {3,5,6,7}.
engine_settings.completion_predicate: requested depth d completed <=> usealphabeta == true AND currentMaxPly == d + 1. Under mdFixedPly=true the loop's only break is guarded by maxTime > 0 and maxTime is -1, so it always runs to completion and exits at maxPly + 1.

budgets.on_timeout: record the query as TIMEOUT, stop measuring deeper depths, and LOG that deeper depths were not measured; never silently truncate

cost_metric.selector_metric_definition: wall-clock milliseconds measured by the HARNESS around the whole child process, including jvm start, class loading and the search
cost_metric.descriptive_only_definition: System.nanoTime around computeMove inside the jvm; recorded per query but NEVER an input to any gate
cost_metric.why_wall: the screen's cost is what the harness must actually wait for, which includes process start; engine time understates it

strong_endpoint_selection_rule.statement: The strong endpoint is the DEEPEST candidate depth d satisfying all three conditions. Selection is by COST ONLY, measured in WALL milliseconds. The moves returned are not an input to this rule.
conditions: every frozen position completed at d, per completion_predicate, within per_query_timeout_s
max observed per-query WALL time across all positions at d <= max_query_ms
projected determinism cost (25 * max observed per-query WALL time at d) <= determinism_budget_s
strong_endpoint_selection_rule.if_only_depth_3_qualifies: strong endpoint == weak endpoint; record that the endpoints coincide as a FINDING, since an endpoint screen between identical settings measures nothing

dial_response_classification.note: Identical moves are NOT proof the dial is dead: a deeper search can correctly re-select the same move.
dial_response_classification.observable_move_response: at least one (position, depth) returns a move different from that position's depth-3 move, and every compared query completed its requested depth
dial_response_classification.no_observed_move_response_inconclusive: every move identical across all measured depths AND every requested depth demonstrably completed
dial_response_classification.dial_failure_stop: any requested depth not completed, or the setting ignored (usealphabeta false, or currentMaxPly != d+1)

positions.min_plies_reason: moveNr >= 6 bypasses InitialMoves, whose firstMove() path uses an UNSEEDED Random
positions.evaluation_regime_note: Evaluation.evaluatePosition zeroes one side's value while match.getMoveNr() < 8, so positions at 6-7 plies sit in a different evaluation regime from positions at 8+. Both regimes are represented.
positions.construction: deterministic scripted sequences verified in our engine before T1j is driven. No agent chooses a move, no search runs during construction, no seeds are consumed.

binding.ply_cap_origin: entirely external to T1j; applied identically to both engines, each engine's ply derived independently
binding.adapter: scripts/GPU/alphazero/t1j_adapter.py, as qualified by E3b attempt 3

determinism_stage.structure: the E3a structure at the SELECTED strong endpoint: 20 independent constructions in ONE jvm plus 5 FRESH jvms, 25 queries total
determinism_stage.process_structure_required: exactly 1 distinct pid across the 20 shared records, exactly 5 DISTINCT pids across the fresh records, 6 processes in all -- asserted from the helper's own PROC lines, not from how the harness believes it invoked them
per_record_requirements: all 25 records persisted individually, not only an aggregate
every record returns the identical legal move and the identical completed depth
EVERY returned state dump re-bound through the same searched-versus-bound E3b comparison used by the sweep, before the aggregate may pass

scoring.draw_definition: the game reached ply_cap 280 with no winner. TwixT cannot draw by rule; a draw here is ALWAYS a cap termination and is recorded as terminal_reason='cap'.
scoring.cap_saturation_abort: if more than half the games at an endpoint terminate by cap, that endpoint is INCOMPLETE: the positions are not resolving and a score rate over them means little

per_endpoint_decision.SATURATED_STRONG: score rate >= 0.95, i.e. T1j score >= 15.2 of 16
per_endpoint_decision.SATURATED_WEAK: score rate <= 0.05, i.e. T1j score <= 0.8 of 16
per_endpoint_decision.INCOMPLETE: fewer than 16 games resolved at this endpoint, or the cap-saturation abort fired

early_stop.rule: stop this endpoint as soon as BOTH saturation verdicts are arithmetically unreachable, and record IN_BAND. Unreachable means: SATURATED_STRONG needs score + (16 - played) >= 15.2, and SATURATED_WEAK needs score <= 0.8.
early_stop.reachability: This CAN fire early and does so quickly: one win and one loss gives score 1 after 2 games, whence 1 + 14 = 15 < 15.2 and 1 > 0.8, so IN_BAND is forced after TWO games.
early_stop.asymmetry_stated_plainly: A SATURATED verdict can never be reached before all 16 games at that endpoint, because 0.95 of 16 exceeds 15 whole points. Only the IN_BAND verdict can stop early. Attempt 1 claimed a saturation early-stop checked every 4 games; with this band and this n that rule could never fire, which is exactly the defect review identified.

joint_outcome.note: computed from the pair (decision_weak, decision_strong); the classifier is total over all 16 combinations and asserts so
joint_outcome.IN_BAND: at least one endpoint IN_BAND and neither INCOMPLETE -- a larger match may be proposed AT THE IN-BAND ENDPOINT(S)
joint_outcome.BRACKETED: one endpoint SATURATED_WEAK and the other SATURATED_STRONG -- the dial spans the band without landing in it, so a usable depth plausibly lies between them; a larger match may be proposed at an intermediate depth
joint_outcome.T1J_TOO_STRONG: both endpoints SATURATED_STRONG -- stop; T1j cannot calibrate against us
joint_outcome.T1J_TOO_WEAK: both endpoints SATURATED_WEAK -- stop; T1j cannot calibrate against us
joint_outcome.INCONCLUSIVE: either endpoint INCOMPLETE -- a larger match may be proposed only after the incompleteness is understood

forbidden: any claim of strength monotonicity from move differences
any claim of strength from timing
any absolute strength placement: T1j is uncalibrated, so even a passing screen yields an ORDERING, not a placement
any per-game runtime figure that assumes a moves-per-game count no measurement supports
